# NTE Capture component source

This headless runtime and minimal D3D12 proxy are produced by UETools-NTE. The supplied GPL v3 and Microsoft Detours MIT notices retain their original terms.

Source base: 1beefcc09c57cbd3872decc666c3c5d5960e9028; working-tree build input SHA-256: 4a44bb9bf0b9bd8b1e29219b821fb4ab7a4122176c35804173e6ac0110cf82b3. Release x64, raw capture evidence enabled. The source base alone does not reproduce this integration build.

The runtime retains read-only inventory, character, team, environment, equipment and pause observations through one native pipe. Character cultivation includes observed base and awakening skill levels, likeability IDs and levels, and equipped fork evidence. Inventory references preserve permanent CARD identities and omit empty equipment cells. Revision checks protect paginated snapshots; asynchronous refresh preserves hit delivery and stop preemption. Frozen pages are copied and serialized by the existing pipe worker. First and terminal pages retain game-thread root validation; every page checks invalidation before copying and after serialization. No public protocol or mutable-object read is moved off the game thread. Bounded arrays use an observation-local bulk copy with per-row fallback on unreadable spans. Float JSON uses locale-independent nine-digit to_chars formatting with unchanged non-finite null semantics.

Native settlement hits carry directly observed player DefaultCharacterID for attacker and victim, and monster configuration IDs separately from instance keys. Missing identities remain null; display names do not establish attribution. Same-root player-state replication and local pawn replacement preserve capture ownership; unknown or changed roots stop capture. Domain changes invalidate only their dependent snapshots: character XP, skills, affinity and fork cultivation refresh character data without invalidating EQUIP inventory. Equipment membership, slots, level/breakthrough and unlock signals retain conservative inventory checks. Satiety and cooldown notifications do not refresh saved build data. Idle connections do not sample the combat clock. Each recording establishes a fresh baseline before start and retains one final sample after stop for Core consumption. Pause continuity follows stable world/controller/player-state roots, independently of team revisions. Effect rows retain bounded evaluated Spec modifier magnitudes and exact definition class paths. Ordinary modifier bindings include attribute names and operation ordinals only when immutable class-default metadata is readable, no custom HT modifier group exists, and counts agree. Custom group counts remain explicit; unknown definitions or mismatches never prove an attack increment. Raw values remain available for diagnostics. The existing hit callback and per-recording metadata cache are reused; no new hook is introduced. Component enumeration reuses validated live-owner field metadata while rereading mutable links and membership on every observation. These changes require game acceptance.

Load through the supplied same-directory D3D12 proxy or a separately verified standard Loader; only one provider may own a game process. Process exit is required for replacement. No development UI, MCP, hot unload, private source, debug symbols or account data is included. Focused wire and lifecycle checks passed. Common-clone request and response observations use bounded local PlayerState RPC messages. A safely copied reset response invalidates configuration after the game callback without closing capture. Restart acceptance in the game for these exact binaries remains pending.
